title: A registered run's verification record settles, but no settlement notice reaches the requesting session, which keeps waiting
outcome: A registered run's verification record settles, but no settlement notice reaches the requesting session, which keeps waiting
acceptance: When a registered run's verification record settles (passed or failed), the requesting session's next turn carries a settlement notice naming the record, even if the run's earlier notice was already delivered, and a session waiting on that run through a run wait is resumed with a prompt that names the settled record; covered by behaviour tests for a failed run. One limit applies to run waits: if the host's latest completed look leaves the record pending for a reason under which it is not sent or settled, namely a route reason (no_connection, capability_unsupported, initiating_session_gone, persist_failed or store_changed), a refusal of the record's body or input (such as body_mismatch), or a record Engram has received that this host cannot yet settle because no launch observation carries it, the wait is resumed naming that reason (and, for a received record, its record ids) instead of the settled record (a wait that has deferred once for a run's look in flight does not defer again for a later look of that run), and a later settlement, if any, then reaches only the run owner's next turn, not a different session that was waiting on the run (tracked as w-d73a959467a1). A second limit applies to what a run wait follows after it resumes: when a wait that ends on any one of several runs resumes, any other run that the host's index does not yet show as finished, and, in any run wait, a run that the resume reports as unknown because its files could not be read at that moment, is reported as such and is not followed further, and that run's later settlement reaches only the run owner's next turn (tracked as w-a6eefa5cc561). A third limit applies to a run that a resumed wait reports as unknown and that the wait is not yet following: if, when the wait decides whether to follow it (having deferred at most once for a look of that run in flight), the host has recorded no look of that run that built its record and Engram has received none, it is not followed further, and its later settlement reaches only the run owner's next turn (tracked as w-a6eefa5cc561). These outcomes assume a run's launcher-written files (its request, results and other run files) are not rewritten or replaced by anything other than the launcher after the run's terminal write; removal of the run directory and files becoming unreadable are otherwise covered, while defence against such rewrites is tracked as w-3c1dd299f0f6. A fourth limit applies to a run wait on a run of another host (a federation wait): it is resumed with the origin host's native verdict, or with a remote conflict when the origin's reported identity or terminal changed, reported uncredited (producer_unsupported), and names no verification record, while destination admission of remote verification records is unavailable; the record's settlement reaches the run owner's next turn on the origin host (tracked as w-26621b52632d).
A session can read a run's settled state through a documented read-only route (for example the launcher's summary) that reports the record id and outcome.
